svg.aria-label: short retention produces a smaller total and no error
svg.text: Surviving a bug fix — and the two assumptions that fail silently
1 fix site · replay 9 events · retention and determinism are assumed, not built
2 // Two of an event's five fields are CLOCKS, which ch01 established:
3 // et = event time, when it happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // v = the value being aggregated · key = the grouping column
5 type Event { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 events, in ARRIVAL order (tools/stream_seed.js).
8 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
9 // primitive: WIN — the window width, in seconds. WIN = 120
10 // primitive: LAG — the watermark's assumed worst-case skew. LAG = 60
11 // primitive: KEYS — the distinct grouping values. KEYS = ["a", "b"]
12 // primitive: TOTAL — the dataset's true total. TOTAL = 45
13 // primitive: append(xs, x) — xs with x added at the end. append([1], 2) = [1,2]
14 // primitive: floorTo(t, w) — t rounded down to a multiple of w.
16 // primitive: watermarkAfter(i) — highest et through i, minus LAG.
23 // primitive: BUG_KEY — the key the bug halves. BUG_KEY = "a"
24 // primitive: buggyV(e) — what the broken pipeline computes for an event.
26 // primitive: nondeterministic(e) — what a pipeline that reads the WALL CLOCK
27 // computes: a value that depends on something outside the log.
30 // function: logWith(retainedCount) — the log, retaining only its last N events.
40 // function: replayThrough(log, pipe) — re-read the retained log through the
41 // pipeline. This is the ONLY recovery mechanism in the design.
53 // function: verify(log, pipe) — can this replay be TRUSTED to reproduce history?
54 // Two assumptions, and each fails without an error.
56 // verify(logWith(6), Pipeline(true, true)).why = "retention shorter than history"
57 // verify(logWith(9), Pipeline(true, false)).why = "pipeline reads outside the log"
60 if (log.retained < len(EVENTS)) { return Outcome(t, false, "retention shorter than history") }
61 if (pipe.deterministic == false) { return Outcome(t, false, "pipeline reads outside the log") }
65 // function: main() — THE CALLER: the healthy replay, and the two silent failures.
Step 2/0 — short retention produces a smaller total and no error
With 6 of 9 events retained the replay returns 30 — a complete, confident, wrong answer. Only this explicit check distinguishes it from 45; the replay itself raises
nothing. "We can always reprocess" is true exactly as far back as retention.
